name: element.list
title: List all elements
summary: Elements of a selection, sorted; optionally as derivation tree or in groups.

selection.description: Every part given must hold (SR-101 AK2).

sort.description: Keys in order: ties go to the next key, then to the workspace order (also without sort). `hierarchy` only first: the list is then the derivation tree, see `tree`. Without sort, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`.

group.description: Group the list (SR-149): `type` (as written, a subtype is a group of its own), `status`, `package` (the property with the meaning `packages`), or the key of a property whose values element.facets offers: a choice or relation property, or a text, number or date property with few values shared in the workspace (a topic, not a title). Whether a text, number or date key can be grouped follows the data of the workspace (the element.facets rule with its default maxValues of 30), so the same key can become input.invalid as the data changes. Any other key is input.invalid. Groups come in the order a sort by the value gives: types, statuses and choices in metamodel order (a choice written by its display name is in the group of that choice), then other values: numbers, texts ignoring case, booleans; packages and other targets by title ignoring case, then short ID (spec-frage #978). Elements without a value form the last group; so do elements whose targets are all not available (`unavailable`). Relation items are read as element.facets and the condition `property eq` read them. An element with several values (packages, a list) is in each of their groups. `sort` (or the saved filter's sort) orders the elements inside each group; with `hierarchy` each group is its own tree. Nothing is stored.

fields.description: Give only these fields of each element (#982), in `partial` instead of `elements`; unlike the `fields` of element.search, which says where to search. `id`, `shortId`, `repository` and the `problems` of an element are always given; a field the element has no value for stays left out, as without `fields`. `text` gives the text as `withText` does, also with `withText` false. Without `fields`, every field in `elements`.

withText.description: Also give the text of each element. Left out for an element without a version, and when its file changed while the list was built (list again).

withVerification.description: Also give what each row shows of its element's verification (SR-137), in `rowVerification`.

elements.description: Without `fields`: one page of the list. With `group`, the page of the grouped list (the elements of the first group, then of the next): an element in several groups is listed once in each, so a page can hold it more than once; key the rows by their position, not by the element.

partial.description: Only with `fields`, instead of `elements`: the same page, each element with the fields asked for.

rowVerification.description: Only with `withVerification`: for each row of `elements` (or `partial`), in the same order, the verification status of a requirement and the progress ring of a requirement or need, as a node of trace.graph carries them (SR-137 AK1, AK3).

tree.description: Only when `sort` starts with `hierarchy` (SR-075 AK2): the place in the derivation tree of each element of `elements` (or `partial`), in the same order. With `group`, each group is its own tree over its elements: a parent outside the group does not count. The list is the tree depth first: each root, then the elements below it. Each element of the selection appears once (spec-frage ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#354): below the parent of the list that reaches it at the shortest depth, the first in sort order among equals; an element without a parent in the list is a root, and so is the first element in sort order of a cycle that no root reaches. Its other parents are in its `relations`.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

depth.description: 0 for a root, 1 for an element below it, and so on.

parent.description: The element it is shown below, a parent of it by a derivation; left out for a root. It may lie on an earlier page.

groups.description: Only with `group`: every group of the whole list in order, also those on other pages; a group without elements is not given. `offset` and `rows` follow from the counts and are given for convenience.

offset.description: Only with `group`: the row the page starts at (the `offset` of the input), so that a page can be headed by its groups without the input.

rows.description: Only with `group`: the rows of the grouped list, the sum of the counts of `groups`; `offset` and `limit` page over these rows. At least `total`, more when elements are in several groups.

total.description: Elements in the selection, each once.
